messages:
elena: Quick heads-up — I tried the canary publish for py/ts SDK (v2.4.0-canary.3) in the 10:00 release window and hit a PyPI signing mismatch on the Python wheel. Deploy log below.

deploy-bot: publish failed — twine exit code 1
stdout:
  Uploading distributions to https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/
stderr:
  HTTPError: 400 Cannot sign release: signature verification failed
  (upload aborted)

sam: ugh. is this the old key rotation fallout? did we rotate the signing key last week?

marco: we rotated the key but key rotation was behind a gate for release pipeline, shouldn't have affected canary. i'll check the signing service (kms-sign) logs.

priya: stop the canary rollout please. do not tag npm canary or update the docs site until we confirm. if npm already got the canary tag, we should remove it.

elena: npm canary publish succeeded earlier (js package got canary tag). py publish failed, so there is now an inconsistent state. suggested actions: remove npm canary tag, hold back the public SDK docs patch, and republish Python with fixed wheel.

sam: to remove tag: `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary` — i'll do that in 2m unless someone objects.

anya: security note — i see a recent artifact signing key rotation for the macos runner (key id: km-7f2b). please verify the twine signing used the correct key and that CI used the right keyring.

marco: confirming logs: kms-sign returned 200 but the signature blob didn't match the wheel metadata — looks like a packaging step inserted extra metadata into the wheel after signing. probable cause: `build_wheel` step added a generated file (docs/_generated) after sign.

sean: ok that explains mismatch. quick fix = rebuild sdist/wheel, sign after build, then twine upload. sam, do you want me to create a hotpatch branch and republish?

sam: yes please. create `hotfix/canary-py-sign` and patch the packaging script to run sign at the end. we'll republish to PyPI with the same version suffix (canary.3) to keep parity. i'll keep npm canary removed until we confirm both published.

priya: timeline/coordination: republish attempt now, then wait 15m for propagation. if successful, we'll re-tag npm canary and push docs. if it fails again, we rollback the canary plan and promote a different canary (canary.2) while we investigate deeper.

sean: pushing PR now and running publish workflow: `./scripts/publish-python --canary --sign-after-build`

deploy-bot: running workflow `publish-python-canary` (#876)
status: in_progress

deploy-bot: workflow complete — success
stdout:
  Built wheel and sdist
  Signed wheel with key km-7f2b
  Uploading distributions...
  Upload complete (v2.4.0-canary.3)

elena: confirmed — PyPI has v2.4.0-canary.3 now. sam, feel free to re-add npm canary and unhold docs.

sam: done — `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.4.0-canary.3 canary` :thumbsup:

priya: decision notes for release log: hold deprecation announcement until next stable publish. record reason = canary instability during packaging; patched; republish succeeded. action items: (1) update release notes with the hotfix entry, (2) notify marketing to delay deprecation banner until next Friday, (3) run a quick smoke test against hosted API with the canary artifacts.

elena: i'll add the release note snippet and kick off the smoke tests. smoke tests ok? reply with :white_check_mark:

sean: smoke tests green + manual sanity checks on examples.

priya: thanks all. closing the hold — will follow up with a short changelog PR and postpone deprecation by one week. if anything else pops up, re-open thread. :rocket:
